summary: US-015: Channel allocations — caps and scheduled release
description:
### US-015: Channel allocations — caps and scheduled release
**As** an organizer, **I want** to split a slot's sellable capacity across sales channels with
per-channel caps and scheduled give-back, so presales and resellers can't starve the public
on-sale. **Priority:** P1 **Depends on:** US-014 (extends the same claim-model surface; soft —
parallelizable if Planning confirms no schema overlap)
**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] A pool can carry channel allocations (opaque channel code + cap + optional release-at
      time); allocations never sum above pool capacity; unallocated capacity is the default/public
      channel.
- [ ] Holds carry a channel; a hold beyond its channel's remaining allocation is rejected even
      when the pool has capacity (and vice-versa: pool exhaustion rejects regardless of channel
      headroom). The no-oversell proof extends to per-channel caps under the contention test.
- [ ] At `release-at`, a channel's unsold allocation returns to the public channel — enforced by
      DB time like TTL expiry (lazy, correct without a sweeper); the release is observable in
      availability reads.
- [ ] Channel codes are opaque strings here; the channel registry, per-channel pricing and
      windows stay in TKT-17/TKT-5 (non-goal).

**Quality gates (every story):**
- `make check` green (lint + unit + integration + smoke; mirrors CI)
- Contract tests pass for any touched service boundary (ADR-009 drift check)
- Money/ticket-path: audit-trail invariants hold (ADR-003)
- Read-endpoint changes: ADR-004 TTL tier declared with rationale

Parent epic: TKT-4. Full lineage: docs/product/prd-v1.md §TKT-4.

objective.note: Epic COS 3: split sellable capacity across channels with caps and scheduled give-back so presales/resellers can't starve the public.

scope.note: IN: allocations (opaque code + cap + release-at) on a pool, channel on holds, dual rejection (channel cap / pool capacity), lazy scheduled release. OUT: channel registry, per-channel pricing/windows (TKT-17/TKT-5).

uncertainties.note: Sub-pool rows vs cap counters is the main design fork — Planning decides against the lock-order rules.

dependencies.note: Soft on US-014 (same claim-model surface); parallelizable if Planning confirms no schema overlap — not wired as a blocker.

approach.note: Allocation table keyed to pool; channel column on claims joins the availability math under the existing pool lock; contention test extends to per-channel caps.

first_slice.note: Allocate 100 of a 1000 pool to 'presale' with release-at T; presale hold 101 rejects; after T the unsold 100 are publicly claimable.

success.note: The 4 ACs + quality gates; per-channel no-oversell under contention is the load-bearing signal.

binding.rule: The inventory database is the sole write-side correctness boundary. Each mutation locks the inventory pool row first, then its claim rows; operations addressed by hold ID discover the pool with a non-locking read, then re-read the claim after locking the pool — every path has the same pool-to-claim lock order. A claim is held, confirmed, released, or expired; the last three are terminal. PostgreSQL time decides expiry: a transaction expires due holds before capacity accounting, so cleanup jobs are optional optimizations. Confirmed plus unexpired-held quantity may never exceed pool capacity. Hold creation requires an organizer-scoped idempotency key, single-use across the claim's full lifecycle. Reserved seats, date ranges, and entitlements reuse the lifecycle and lock ordering but add their own resource constraints.

governingAdrs.why: Channel caps are a second accounting dimension inside the same pool lock — lazy DB-time release mirrors hold expiry (sweep before accounting, no sweeper needed for correctness).
Allocation config + channel on holds change the OpenAPI contract and possibly the hold request fingerprint — idempotency replay semantics must stay exact.

**Plan draft — authored by gpt-5.6-sol (codex task 019f6b3d-7123-73f3-aef8-3bfbd04a7929), read-only run.**

## Design decision

Choose **allocation rows with derived usage**, not materialized sub-pools or mutable counters.

- Add `channel_allocations`, keyed by `(pool_id, channel_code)`, containing `cap` and nullable `release_at`.
- Keep `inventory_pools` as the single serialization point. Allocation administration and every claim mutation lock the pool row first; allocation and claim rows are only read or changed afterward.
- Reject sub-pools because one sale would need to coordinate parent and child capacity, introducing another lock order and complicating atomic give-back.
- Do not store consumed counters. Derive channel consumption from confirmed plus live (`held`/`finalizing`) channel-attributed claims under the pool lock. This prevents counter/claim drift.
- Represent release solely through the DB-time predicate:

  ```sql
  release_at IS NULL OR release_at > now()
  ```

  No allocation sweep, released flag, or background job is required. The row may remain for configuration visibility, but it no longer reserves capacity.

- The public/default channel is implicit: `claims.channel_code IS NULL`. It has no allocation row.
- Allocation administration is an atomic full-set replacement through `PUT /internal/slots/{id}/channel-allocations`. This avoids transient capacity exposure when moving cap from one channel to another.
- New channel holds require a matching active allocation. At or after `release_at`, new holds for that channel return `409`; existing holds may still finalize/confirm because they already consumed capacity before release.
- Channel codes are exact opaque values: no registry lookup, case folding, or normalization.

Accounting under the pool lock:

- `global_remaining = capacity - confirmed_quantity - live_claims`
- For active allocation `i`, `consumed_i = confirmed claims + live claims` carrying that channel.
- `channel_available_i = max(0, min(global_remaining, cap_i - consumed_i))`
- `public_available = max(0, global_remaining - Σ(active cap_i - consumed_i))`

This returns only each active channel’s unsold reservation at release, while existing held/confirmed quantities remain globally consumed.

Operational-hold policy:

- Operational holds remain unchanneled and consume only global pool capacity. They can therefore cause pool exhaustion while a channel still has nominal cap headroom.
- Conversion creates a public/default buyer hold (`channel_code = NULL`). It bypasses a public-capacity check because the conversion is quantity-neutral under the pool lock; if the child expires, ADR-023’s existing rule returns that quantity to public capacity.
- Operational place/release/convert audit behavior remains unchanged.

Idempotency:

- `channel` joins the buyer `CreateHold` fingerprint because changing it changes the constrained allocation. Same key and same channel replays; same key with a different or omitted channel conflicts.
- Preserve the existing fingerprint byte-for-byte when channel is absent so claims created before migration remain replayable. Only channel-bearing requests use the extended canonical input.
- Allocation administration uses idempotent `PUT`, not an idempotency-key registry: the body is the complete desired set, and repeating it leaves the same committed state.

Record these choices in `ADR-024-channel-allocations.md`, including the ADR-004 availability TTL declaration.

## DoD

- Pools accept an atomic set of zero or more channel allocations whose caps sum to at most pool capacity.
- Public holds cannot consume unreleased channel reservations; channel holds cannot exceed their cap; neither can exceed global pool capacity.
- Channel attribution survives hold replay and every buyer lifecycle transition.
- PostgreSQL `now()` activates give-back without a sweeper, and availability reflects it within the declared five-second cache tier.
- Operational holds remain pool-only; conversion produces a public/default buyer hold without exposing capacity.
- Allocation configuration is internal-token protected and unavailable through the gateway.
- Claim creation and transitions continue to append `claim_history`; no claim is rewritten to change its channel.
- No channel registry, pricing/window policy, allocation counters, sweeper, or domain event is introduced.
- `make generate` produces committed contract models with no drift.
- `make check` passes.

## Schema/migration

Add `services/inventory/internal/store/migrations/0004_channel_allocations.sql`:

- Create `channel_allocations`:

  - `pool_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES inventory_pools(slot_id)`
  - `channel_code text NOT NULL`
  - `cap integer NOT NULL CHECK (cap > 0)`
  - `release_at timestamptz NULL`
  - timestamps
  - primary key `(pool_id, channel_code)`
  - length/non-empty check matching the OpenAPI limit.

- Add nullable `claims.channel_code`; existing rows become public/default without a backfill.
- Extend `claims_kind_shape` so operational claims must have `channel_code IS NULL`.
- Do not add a foreign key from claims to allocations: removing an allocation must close the channel without destroying historical claim attribution.
- Add a plain index such as:

  ```sql
  CREATE INDEX claims_pool_channel_status_expiry
      ON claims(pool_id, channel_code, status, expires_at);
  ```

  This follows ADR-020; no `CONCURRENTLY`.

Cross-row cap sums cannot be expressed as a PostgreSQL `CHECK`. `ReplaceChannelAllocations` will:

1. Lock `inventory_pools ... FOR UPDATE`.
2. Read channel consumption from claims.
3. Validate unique codes, positive caps, each included cap not below its current confirmed/live consumption, and the total using `int64`.
4. Replace the set within that transaction.

Omitting a channel closes/releases it immediately; existing claims remain valid and globally counted. Re-adding that code later must accommodate its still-confirmed/live claims.

The down migration should refuse to discard non-public claim attribution silently if any `channel_code` remains populated.

## Files to change

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `docs/adr/ADR-024-channel-allocations.md` | Record row-vs-sub-pool decision, accounting formulas, release policy, operational policy, idempotency, and five-second TTL tier. |
| `services/inventory/internal/store/migrations/0004_channel_allocations.sql` | Add allocation table, claim channel, shape constraint, and plain index. |
| `services/inventory/internal/store/store.go` | Add channel to `Claim`; extend fingerprint/CreateHold; centralize channel/global accounting; make public availability channel-aware. |
| `services/inventory/internal/store/channel_allocations.go` | Allocation types, atomic full-set replacement, DB-time availability calculations. |
| `services/inventory/internal/store/operational.go` | Return channel breakdown in staff availability; explicitly create converted children with the public/default channel. |
| `services/inventory/internal/api/server.go` | Decode/return channel on holds; accept optional availability channel; register allocation route. |
| `services/inventory/internal/api/operational.go` | Internal allocation handler and expanded staff availability response. |
| `services/inventory/api/openapi.yaml` | Contract changes described below. |
| `services/inventory/internal/api/openapi_gen.go` | Regenerated inventory models. |
| `services/commerce/api/openapi.yaml` | Add optional channel to reservation creation so the existing purchasable flow can reach channel inventory. |
| `services/commerce/internal/api/openapi_gen.go` | Regenerated commerce models. |
| `services/commerce/internal/api/server.go` | Forward optional channel unchanged to inventory; omitted remains public/default. |
| `services/commerce/internal/api/server_test.go` | Pin exact channel forwarding and omitted-channel behavior. |
| `services/inventory/internal/api/server_test.go` | Allocation authentication and request-shape tests; channel validation. |
| `services/inventory/internal/store/channel_allocations_smoke_test.go` | Real-Postgres accounting, release, migration, idempotency, and overflow tests. |
| `services/inventory/internal/store/operational_smoke_test.go` | Pin pool-only operational behavior and public-channel conversion. |
| `smoke/inventory_contention_test.go` | Extend composed-stack contention proof to channel and public limits. |

No consumer, Compose, migration runner, or domain-event files change.

## Test seam & test plan

Use real-Postgres store smoke tests as the primary correctness seam. The transaction, DB clock, predicates, and row locks are the behavior under test; handler mocks cannot prove them.

### AC 1 — configuration and implicit public capacity

- Configure multiple allocations and verify their sum plus implicit public capacity.
- Reject a replacement whose caps exceed pool capacity; verify the prior set remains unchanged.
- Reject lowering an included cap below its confirmed/live usage.
- Verify empty allocation set makes the whole remaining pool public.
- Verify allocation replacement is atomic under the pool lock.
- Exercise `math.MaxInt32` capacity with caps whose `int32` sum would wrap; the `int64` validation must reject them.

### AC 2 — dual limits and contention

- Channel-cap rejection with global pool headroom.
- Public rejection while active channel reservations still have headroom.
- Pool-exhaustion rejection while the requested channel has cap headroom, using operational or other-channel consumption.
- Exact replay with the same channel returns the original claim.
- Same key with another channel, or channel versus omitted channel, returns `ErrIdempotency`.
- Pin the legacy/no-channel fingerprint so migration does not invalidate existing idempotency records.
- Confirm/finalize/release a channel hold and verify its channel remains unchanged and claim-history actions remain complete.
- Extend `TestInventoryContentionSafeHolds` with a capacity-10 pool, channel cap 6, and concurrent channel/public requests. Assert exactly six channel grants, four public grants, ten total, and no unexpected status.
- Retain the existing global and operational conversion contention proofs.

### AC 3 — lazy scheduled release

- Create an allocation with a near-future DB timestamp and consume part of it.
- Before release, assert channel and public availability reserve the unsold channel quantity.
- Poll only read endpoints until PostgreSQL time crosses `release_at`; run no mutation or sweep.
- Assert channel availability becomes zero and public availability increases by exactly the unsold allocation.
- Assert existing channel holds still transition normally after release.
- Verify `Cache-Control: public, max-age=5, s-maxage=5`.

### AC 4 — opaque codes

- Distinct case-sensitive codes remain distinct.
- Codes pass unchanged through commerce, inventory, persistence, responses, and fingerprints.
- Unknown/released channel holds reject without any registry lookup.
- Contract validation rejects only structural violations such as missing/empty/overlength codes, not invented channel semantics.

### Boundary and regression tests

- OpenAPI request validation for allocation replacement, hold channel, and optional availability query.
- Response validation for public and staff availability shapes.
- Internal credential required and empty credential fails closed.
- Gateway continues returning 404 for the new `/internal/` route.
- Served contracts remain byte-identical to committed files.
- Existing unchanneled checkout and operational-conversion smoke tests remain green.
- Migration from existing public claims preserves `NULL` channel and replay behavior.
- `claim_history` UPDATE/DELETE rejection remains pinned.

## API/contract changes

Inventory:

- `HoldCreate`: optional `channel`.
- `Hold`: optional `channel`; absent means public/default.
- `GET /slots/{id}/availability`: optional `channel` query parameter.

  - Without it, `available` is public/default claimable capacity.
  - With it, `available` is claimable capacity for that exact channel.
  - `capacity`, `held`, and `confirmed` remain pool aggregates.
  - Unknown or released channels report `available: 0`.
  - The endpoint remains in ADR-004’s five-second remaining-capacity tier.

- `PUT /internal/slots/{id}/channel-allocations`: internal-token-protected atomic replacement:

  ```json
  {
    "organizer_id": "uuid",
    "allocations": [
      {
        "channel": "presale.partner-a",
        "cap": 250,
        "release_at": "2026-09-01T14:00:00Z"
      }
    ]
  }
  ```

  An empty array removes all active allocation reservations. Return the committed configuration with `200`; structural errors use `400`, and capacity/consumption conflicts use `409`.

- `StaffAvailability`: retain top-level global `available`, add `public_available` and channel entries containing `channel`, `cap`, optional `release_at`, derived `released`, `held`, `confirmed`, and `available`. Staff reads remain `no-store`.

Commerce:

- `ReservationCreate` gains the same optional opaque `channel` and forwards it unchanged to inventory. No commerce schema column is needed: inventory owns allocation enforcement and attribution.
- Existing callers omit it and remain on the public/default channel.

No event contract changes are needed.

## Risks & open questions

- Public `Availability.available` becomes sellable-to-requested-channel rather than raw global remainder when allocations exist. That is the useful buyer-facing meaning, but it is a semantic contract change and must be called out in ADR-024.
- The five-second cache tier means release visibility may lag DB time by up to five seconds on reads. Write correctness still switches exactly at PostgreSQL time.
- This plan treats release as closing the allocated channel for new holds; it does not let that channel spill into public inventory afterward. Such spillover is a channel-window policy and belongs with TKT-17/TKT-5.
- Full-set `PUT` is state-idempotent but has no stale-write protection: a delayed older request can replace a newer set. Versioning or `If-Match` is not required by this story; add it only if concurrent organizer editing is in scope.
- Allocation configuration changes do not enter `claim_history`: they are sellability configuration, not claim lifecycle mutations. Channel attribution itself is immutable on each claim, and all existing claim-history invariants remain. If “who changed allocation configuration” is required, it should be shaped explicitly rather than hidden in claim history.
- Derived sums add indexed claim aggregation to the serialized write path. This preserves correctness and avoids counter drift; TKT-82 remains the appropriate place to measure whether materialized counters are ever justified.

<!-- sdlc:stage=plan-review kind=plan-final -->
**Plan critique + final plan — critic/finalizer: main-agent** (draft by gpt-5.6-sol). Drive style is gates-only, so open decisions were resolved by the critic with recorded rationale instead of grilling the human.

## Critique verdicts (per part of the draft)

1. **Allocation rows + derived usage, implicit public channel, DB-time release predicate** — ACCEPT. Verified against store.go: single pool-lock serialization preserved (ADR-010), `release_at > now()` mirrors the `liveClaims` expiry pattern, zero background jobs. Derived sums (no counters) also self-heal on hold expiry — sweepExpired flips the claim, the sum follows.
2. **`PUT /internal/slots/{id}/channel-allocations` atomic full-set replacement** — ACCEPT. State-idempotent; stale-write risk accepted as the draft states (single-organizer admin, out of scope).
3. **Channel joins the CreateHold fingerprint; legacy fingerprint byte-exact when channel absent** — ACCEPT, with the pinning test the draft already lists (ADR-009 replay exactness).
4. **Operational holds unchanneled; `claims_kind_shape` extended to force `channel_code IS NULL` on operational; convert produces public buyer holds** — ACCEPT. Verified constraint lives in 0003; 0004 must drop + re-add it.
5. **Commerce contract change (ReservationCreate channel + forwarding + tests, 4 files)** — AMEND: CUT. No AC exercises commerce; the contention smoke drives `gateway /api/inventory/holds` directly (verified in smoke/inventory_contention_test.go), and nothing can populate a channel until the channel registry/windows exist (TKT-17/TKT-5 — the ticket's explicit non-goal). Commerce plumbing lands with TKT-17. Shrinks the diff by 4 files; no backlog ticket needed since TKT-17 already owns the surface.
6. **Public availability semantics become channel-scoped claimable (`?channel=` optional)** — ACCEPT. AC 3 observability requires it; must be called out in ADR-024 as a semantic contract change.
7. **ADR-024 + migration 0004 + index** — ACCEPT (plain CREATE INDEX per ADR-020).
8. **Test plan** — ACCEPT with one amendment: the AC-3 lazy-release proof lives in the store smoke seam (near-future DB timestamp, poll reads only), NOT the composed smoke suite — a wall-clock wait in the composed stack is a flake magnet; the composed smoke covers AC 2 contention only.

**Seam verification:** all files/symbols named by the draft exist at HEAD (`TestInventoryContentionSafeHolds`, `claims_kind_shape`, `StaffAvailability`, `make generate`, gateway `/internal/` 404, 5s cache tier at internal/api/server.go:136). No hallucinated seams. Draft's Risks read against its Decision: no self-refutation.

## Pre-mortem (named lens)

Assume Gate 2/3 bounce — most plausible causes: (a) contention assertion nondeterminism — checked: with cap 6 of capacity 10, public claimable is exactly 4 regardless of interleaving, so "exactly 6 channel + 4 public grants" is deterministic; (b) per-channel sums written against a hand-rolled expiry predicate instead of `liveClaims` — store.go's comment names this exact trap, so the plan now REQUIRES channel consumption to derive from the `liveClaims` predicate; (c) migration forgetting the drop/re-add of `claims_kind_shape` — named explicitly above. Lens changed: added the liveClaims requirement, pinned the AC-3 seam to store smoke.

## Final plan = draft as posted, minus commerce (item 5), plus:

- Per-channel consumption MUST be computed with the shared `liveClaims` predicate (store.go:61) — never a re-derived expiry expression.
- Migration 0004: drop + re-add `claims_kind_shape` including `channel_code IS NULL` on the operational arm; nullable `claims.channel_code`; `channel_allocations` table; plain composite index.
- AC-3 release test in `channel_allocations_smoke_test.go` (store seam, real Postgres, ~1–2s release_at horizon); composed smoke extension limited to the mixed-channel contention proof.
- Files to change: draft's table minus the 3 commerce rows and its openapi regen; everything else stands.

## Introduced at plan-review, reviewed by no second model

- Cutting the commerce scope (item 5) — deferral to TKT-17.
- The explicit `liveClaims`-reuse requirement for channel sums.
- Pinning the AC-3 test to the store smoke seam instead of the composed suite.

These reach Gate 2 reviewed only by their author (main-agent); flagged again at the Gate 3 hand-off.

<!-- sdlc:stage=coding kind=summary -->
**Implementation — by main-agent (TDD).** PR: https://github.com/mathd/ticketing_system/pull/54

Tests written first (7 store smoke tests + 3 API shape tests + 1 composed contention test), then the implementation per the approved plan-final:

- `0004_channel_allocations.sql` — allocation table, nullable `claims.channel_code`, `claims_kind_shape` extended (operational = unchanneled), composite index (plain CREATE INDEX per ADR-020), guarded down-migration.
- `store/channel_allocations.go` — `ReplaceChannelAllocations` (atomic full-set under pool lock, int64 sum + per-channel consumption validation), `activeAllocation`/`consumingClaims` predicates built ON the shared `liveClaims` (the plan's hard requirement), staff channel breakdown.
- `store.go` — channel joins CreateHold (dual headroom checks under the same pool lock), fingerprint extended with byte-exact legacy form, channel-scoped `Availability`.
- API + OpenAPI — `channel` on HoldCreate/Hold, `?channel=` availability param, internal `PUT .../channel-allocations`, StaffAvailability additions; models regenerated.
- ADR-024 recorded.

One deviation while greening: dropped a redundant in-test gateway-404 assertion (route already pinned by `TestGatewayDeniesGenericInternalRoutes`; a GET on the PUT-only route trips the contract helper with 405).

Local gate `make check` green (exit 0) on the committed tree, run by main-agent.
